title: WPSB/298/2017 of Mahavir Singh Rawat AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (SB) No. 298 of 2017
Mahavir Singh Rawat & another. ............ Petitioners
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .............. Respondents
Writ Petition (SB) No. 299 of 2017
Vivek Kumar Tamta & others. ............ Petitioners
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .............. Respondents
Writ Petition (SB) No. 300 of 2017
Jaydeep Kishore. ............ Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .............. Respondents
&
Writ Petition (SB) No. 301 of 2017
Smt. Ittee Teli. ............ Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .............. Respondents
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Chief Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand / respondent
No. 1.
Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya, Advocate for respondent Nos. 2 to 4 / College.

JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Dated: 6th December, 2017
K.M. JOSEPH, C.J. (Oral)
 These writ petitions, four in number, raise certain common issues
and, hence, we are disposing of the same by this common judgment.

2
2. Advertisement dated 08.06.2013 was issued by the third
respondent, which is a College affiliated with the Uttarakhand Technical
University. The Advertisement was issued calling for applications for
teaching faculties in three streams, namely, (i) Engineering (ii) MCA &
(iii) Applied Sciences and Humanities. It appears that an interview took
place sometime in January, 2014. However, on the basis of a report by a
Committee, the Minister, who is also the Chairman of the Committee,
which manages the College, by order dated 08.06.2015, proceeded to
cancel the entire selection. This, in turn, came to be questioned by the
petitioners in Writ Petition (S/B) No. 253 of 2015. The said writ petition
came to be disposed of on 09.12.2015 on the basis of the following
observations inter alia and directions:
"9. Sri B.D. Kandpal, learned Deputy Advocate General
for the State of Uttarakhand and Sri Subhash Upadhyay, Advocate
for respondent no. 3 and 4 would submit that there were materials
justifying the cancellation of the selection. As regards the invoking
of the emergency powers, nothing much is forthcoming from the
learned Deputy Advocate General or the learned counsel for
respondent nos. 3 and 4 to deny strength to the submissions made
by the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners.
10. We are also of the view that in the facts of this case, there
was no occasion for the Minister to invoke the powers under Clause
32(5) of the Byelaws. 'Emergency power' as the very words
suggest is not to be exercised in routine fashion. The powers are
ordinarily to be exercised by the Board of Governors, which
appears to be a composite body consisting of bureaucrats,
representatives of the Government and Scientific persons. In such
circumstances, particularly in the matter of such moment affecting
so many persons, the question as to whether an extreme decision
should be taken, namely, to cancel the entire selection should
certainly have been discussed and debated by the Members of the
Governing Body in ordinary circumstances. The fact that the
decision is taken after a lapse of nearly a year of the submission of
the report would itself show that there was ample time for the
Board of Governors to discuss the matter and to arrive at a legal
and fair decision. Instead, in our view, the Chairman has exercised
power beyond the scope of the authority conferred on him under the
Byelaw in the facts of this case. In such circumstances, we would
think that the matter should receive the attention of the competent
body, namely, the Board of Governors. In the light of this
discussion, the impugned order has to perish and we must quash it.
11. The question arises further as to whether we quash the
decision as a whole. Petitioners, as we have already noted, have

3
subjected themselves to selection in three different streams. We
would think that the Board of Governors must bestow their
attention as to whether the cancellation of selection in regard to the
disciplines in question, for which the petitioners have offered
themselves for selection, has to be done. To that extent, the writ
petition must be allowed. Accordingly, we allow the writ petition.
The decision dated 08.06.2015 taken by the Chairman will stand
quashed to the extent it relates to the disciplines of the petitioners,
namely, for the posts of Assistant Professor (Mechanical
Engineering), Assistant Professor (Civil Engineering) and Assistant
Professor (Electronics and Communication Engineering). The
Board of Governors will consider the question as to whether,
having regard to the report submitted by the Committee and any
other relevant facts, the selection in regard to the posts, for which
the petitioners have offered themselves for selection, should be
cancelled. A decision in this regard must be taken within a period
of two months from today. We also direct that one post of Assistant
Professor (Mechanical Engineering), one post of Assistant
Professor (Electronics and Communication Engineering) and one
post of Assistant Professor (Civil Engineering) will be kept vacant
till a decision is taken by the Board of Governors. Needless to say,
the Board of Governors will bear in mind the law as declared by the
Hon'ble Apex Court while deciding the issue."
3. Thereafter, we may set out the following sequence of facts:
i. In the 21st Meeting of the Board of Governors dated 22.04.2016,
with two persons as special invitees to the Board and five members of the
Board of Governors absent, a four-member "Sub-Committee" was
constituted. The Sub-Committee gave its report (Annexure No. 3). It
enlisted various transgressions in the matter of screening and also by the
selection committee itself. Apparently, placing reliance on the said
report, in the 22nd Meeting of the Board of Governors dated 03.05.2016, a
decision was taken to cancel the entire selection. Thereafter, it appears
that, by Annexure No. 5 dated 26.05.2016, one R.K. Singh, who was the
member of the Board of Governors, wrote the following letter to the
Principal Secretary:
"To, Date: 26/05/2016
The Principal Secretary/Vice-Chairman,
Board of Governors,
G.B. Pant Engineering College,
Pauri-Garhwal,

4
Subject: Regarding the complaint received against the
misrepresentation of facts about the selection process before Board
of Governors in the 22nd meeting held on 03/05/2016.
Sir,
It is to submit you that I have received a complaint regarding the
fabricated and misleading information about the selection process
presented during 22nd meeting of Board of Governors held on
03/05/2016. Sir, it is to inform you that documents attached as
annexures with the complaint seems different from the documents
produced at the time of BOG meeting by officiating Principal Dr.
Y. Singh and Officiating Registrar Dr. A. K. Gautam. Sir if it is so,
matter seems to be very serious and may be considered for further
investigation.
 Thanking you with regards.
Prof R.K. Singh
Director, BTKIT, Dwarahat
Almora (UK)"
ii. This was followed by Annexure No. 6 dated 30.05.2016, which is a
communication sent by the Vice Chancellor Prof. P.K. Garg to the
Principal Secretary. It reads as follows:
"Date: 30/05/2016
To,
The Principal Secretary,
Technical Education Department,
Government of Uttarakhand,
Dehradun (UK)
Subject: Regarding the decision of cancelling the entire selection
process taken by Board of Governors, G.B. Pant Engineering
College, in the 22nd meeting held on 03/05/2016.
Sir,
With due respect I would like to draw your attention towards
the decision of cancelling of entire selection process taken by
Board of Governors (BOG), G. B. Pant Engineering College, in the
22nd meeting held on 03/05/2016. The decision taken by the BOG
members was based on the facts presented by Dr. Y. Singh,
Officiating Principal, Member Secretary BOG, Dr. H. Goel,
Professor ASHD, nominated member BOG and Dr. A. K. Gautam,
Registrar, G. B. Pant Engineering College.

5
In this regard, I have received a complaint dated 26/05/2016
with the documentary proof as annexures. While going through all
the documents attached with the above complaint and papers
available in agenda of 22nd BOG meeting, I observed that Dr. Y.
Singh and Dr. H. Goel were the part of the screening committees
and selection committees for their departments in 2013-14
(Annexure-1). Since their signatures are present on the document,
it is presumed that they agreed to the data given in Anneuxre . Dr.
A. K. Gautam, now Officiating Registrar, GBPEC was himself a
candidate for the post of Professor, ECE, and was screened out
because he did not have M. Tech Degree (Annexure-2). The
anomalies raised by these members before BOG members were
therefore false and fabricated.
1. The Horizontal reservation is distributed among the
following categories - WOMEN (30%), FF (2%), Ex-Servicemen (5%), Physically Handicapped (3%) etc. The
percentage of this type of reservation is distributed across the
vertical reservation. However as per the rule mentioned in
the order no. 563/KARMIK-2/2002 in paras 3 & 4
(Annexure-3), it is understood that if a woman candidate is
not available the post can be filled by male applicant and it
will not be carried forward further. The information given
that the vacancy was not reserved for the women is baseless
and it appears that proper horizontal reservation was
followed. The reservation of Uttarakhand Andolankari which
has been mentioned in the chart (Annexure-4) produced by
Dr. Y. Singh and Dr. A. K. Gautam before BOG members,
has already been stayed by the honorable High Court in the
year 2011 and the same has not passed by the cabinet, as far
as I know. However out of 42 positions advertised, only 19
candidates have been recommended to be appointed, so still
various positions are lying vacant against which suitable
candidates under various horizontally reserved categories
may be selected in future interviews.
2. Dr. H.Goel, Head, Applied Science & Humanities was the
member of screening and selection committees for ASHD,
including mathematics, and his signature is present on
screening committee minutes (Annexure-5), it shows his
concurrence.
3. As per the AICTE norms (Gazette No. 37-
3/Legal/AICTE/2012), candidates selected for the post of
Professor, Civil Engineering and Associate Professor,
Computer Sc. And Engineering (Dr. H. S. Bhaduria), both
claimed more than 400 API and 300 API, respectively
(Annexure-6). On further examining by myself, it was
observed that the capping system for API calculation which
was produced by Member-Secretary/Principal and Registrar
during BOG meeting and later to sub-committee is applicable
to only Applied Science & Humanities disciplines (As per
UGC G.O. No. F 1-2/2009 (EC/PS) V(I) Vol.II) and not in
Engineering Disciplines (Annexure-70

6
4. The daughter of Dr. M.P.S. Chauhan, Head Civil
Engineering was an applicant due to which he has expressed
his inability in writing to be a part of selection-screening
committee. Thus, the constitution of screening/selection
committee was as per college bye-laws (Annexure-8)
5. As per prevailing rules of AICTE at that time, minimum
qualifications for the post of Professor was B. Tech, M. Tech
and PhD. Dr. A. K. Gautam was not found eligible by
screening committee as he did not have M. Tech Degree.
(Annexure-9)
6. The screening committee did not call Mr. Hitesh Dimri for
interview since the committee found that his M. Tech degree
was not completed. His certificate given by NIT Rourkela
also mentions that "It may be considered as Course
Completion Certificate. It is important to note here that M.
Tech is competed by Court work, followed by one year
Dissertation. It means his dissertation was not completed by
the time of applying for the posts. (Annexure-10)
7. The selection committee was duly constituted by the Govt.,
which consisted of senior and experienced experts of the
respective fields from reputed institutions. The score sheets
and findings of Selection Committee may be given due
weightage and respect. In all selection committee, it is
always a collective decision.
8. The minutes of the 22nd Board of Governors meeting are not
yet circulated by the Member-Secretary/Principal of the
college to me for information and viewing.
It would be better, if the entire case is re-examined once again by
an independent committee not connected with the screening and
selection process, in light of documents attached with this letter vis-à-vis points raised by Dr. Y Singh and Dr. A. K. Gautam in 21st
BOG meeting. Thus, it is requested to please consider the above
mentioned facts before finalizing the minutes of the meeting or any
other proceedings.
Thanking you with kind regards.
Yours Sincerely,
Prof. P.K. Garg
Vice Chancellor"
iii. Annexure No. 7 is the Minutes of the 23rd Meeting of the Board of
Governors, which took place on 19.11.2016. The Board of Governors
proceeded to confirm the decision taken in the 22nd Meeting of the Board
of Governors and it was resolved that, in regard to the selection being
cancelled, unless the Law Department takes a different view, the

7
cancellation be done and, in case the Law Department takes a different
view, the matter again be listed before the Board of Governors.
Thereafter, the 25th Meeting of the Board of Governors, which took place
on 24.05.2017, confirmed the minutes of the 23rd & 24th meetings of the
Board of Governors. Thereafter, it is stated as follows:
"25.05 Discussion and decision on the advertisement
number 01/Faculty/2013-14.
Governing council took the decision that screening
will be done again of all the candidates who applied through
the above mentioned advertisement and the selection process
will be started again and completed within 45 days.
Advice on the legal aspects of the selection process
can be taken from legal advisor Shri S.K. Gupta and
additional Secretary, Judicial, Shri Mahesh Kaushiba as and
when required. After the completion of the selection process
the Minutes of the Meeting (MOM) of the selection
committee will be presented in the next meeting of the
governing council for approval."
4. Petitioners in Writ Petition (S/B) No. 298 of 2017, as already noted,
were the petitioners in the earlier writ petition also, which culminated in
the judgment, pursuant to which, the Board of Governors has proceeded
to consider the matter afresh. The reliefs, which are sought in Writ
Petition (S/B) No. 298 of 2017, are as follows:
"I. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the minutes of 21st, 22nd, 23rd and 25th meeting of
Board of Governors held on 22.04.2016, 03.05.2016,
19.11.2016 and 24-05-2017 along with the report of four
members sub-committee constituted illegally in 21st meeting
of BOG held on 22.04.2016, so far as it relates to the
selection initiated pursuant to the advertisement No. 1/faculty
/ admin/ 2013/14 dated 08-06-2013, so far as it relates to the
Engineering stream.
II. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing to the respondents to implement the
recommendation of the selection committee with immediate
effect by issuing appointment letter to each of the petitioner
on the post of Assistant Professor in engineering stream."

8
5. Petitioners in Writ Petition (S/B) No. 299 of 2017 are six in number
and are applicants for the posts in the Engineering Stream, who claim that
they have been selected by the earlier selection committee. The reliefs,
which have been sought in this writ petition, are as follows:
"I. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the minutes of 21st, 22nd, 23rd and 25th meeting of
Board of Governors held on 22.04.2016, 03.05.2016,
19.11.2016 and 24-05-2017 along with the report of four
members sub-committee constituted illegally in 21st meeting
of BOG held on 22.04.2016, so far as it relates to the
selection initiated pursuant to the advertisement No. 1/faculty
/ admin/ 2013/14 dated 08-06-2013, so far it relates to the
engineering stream.
II. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the earlier decision of the Chairman dated 08-06-
2015 keeping in view of the observation made by this
Hon'ble Court in its Judgment dated 09-12-2015 passed in
writ petition No. 253 (S/B) of 2015 and also keeping in view
of the subsequent decision taken by the Board of Governor in
its 25th meeting held on 24th May 2017.
III. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing to the respondents to implement the
recommendation of the selection committee with immediate
effect by issuing appointment letter to each of the petitioner
on the post of Assistant Professor in engineering stream."
6. Writ Petition (S/B) No. 300 of 2017 is filed by one petitioner, who
lays claim to the post of Assistant Professor in MCA. He also claims to
have been selected by the selection committee and he seeks the similar
reliefs, as are sought in Writ Petition (S/B) No. 299 of 2017.
7. The last remaining writ petition, namely, Writ Petition (S/B) No.
301 of 2017 is filed by the candidate, who was selected for the post of
Assistant Professor in Electronics and Communications. The following
reliefs are sought in the said writ petition:
"I. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the minutes of 21st, 22nd, 23rd and 25th meeting of
Board of Governors held on 22.04.2016, 03.05.2016,
19.11.2016 and 24-05-2017 along with the report of four
members sub-committee constituted illegally in 21st meeting
of BOG held on 22.04.2016, so far as it relates to the

9
selection initiated pursuant to the advertisement No. 1/faculty
/ admin/ 2013/14 dated 08-06-2013.
II. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the report of four members subcommittee
(Annexure No. 3) which is the basis of the decision taken by
the Board of Governors in its 25th meeting held on 24th May
2017.
III. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the earlier decision of the Chairman dated 08-06-
2015 keeping in view of the observation made by this
Hon'ble Court in its Judgment dated 09-12-2015 passed in
writ petition No. 253 (S/B) of 2015 and also keeping in view
of the subsequent decision taken by the Board of Governor in
its 25th meeting held on 24th May 2017.
IV. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing to the respondents to implement the
recommendation of the selection committee with immediate
effect by issuing appointment letter to the petitioner on the
post of Assistant Professor in "engineering stream"."
8. Pleadings have been exchanged. We have heard Mr. Rakesh
Thapliyal, learned counsel for the petitioners in all the writ petitions; Mr.
Subhash Upadhyaya, learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos. 2 to 4
/ College; and Mr. Paresh Tripathi, learned Chief Standing Counsel
appearing for the State.
9. We deem it appropriate to refer in detail to the recommendations of
the Sub-Committee. They are as follows:
"REPORT OF THE SUB-COMMITTEE CONSTITUTED BY THE
BOARD OF GOVERNERS OF G B PANT ENGINEERING
COLLEGE, PAURI GARHWAL
In the meeting of the sub-committee, the following facts
were found:
1. Advertisement was published on 8 June 2013 for the various
faculty positions in the college in various disciplines
(Annexure-3.1) in which the qualification and experience for
engineering positions were as per AICTE norms and for
Applied Sciences as per UGC norms.
2. Total number of the applications received, for various
disciplines are as follows:

3. The screening committee screened out 232 candidates as per
Annexure-3.2. The summary of recommended candidates for
various disciplines is as given below:

Cadre ECE CSE EE ME BT CE MCA ASHD Total
Professor 0 1 0 0 0 2 2 - 5

4. As per recommendation of the screening committee,
interview letters were sent to the candidates, interview letters
of the petitioners are annexed herewith as Annexure-3.3 (3
Nos.) for ready reference.
5. List of selected candidates by the selection committee is as
per Annexure-3.4.
In the above recommendations, the anomalies noticed are as
under:

(i) Anomalies in reservation- as per Annexure-3.5
 (ii) Anomalies in screening- as per Annexure-3.6
 (iii) Anomalies in the selection- as per Annexure-3.7
Observations of the committee are:
(i) The AICTE/UGC norms (as per the advertisement) clearly
provided the following criteria for selection of a candidate
(Annexure-3.8):
Assistant Professor
 a) Academic Records and research performance- 50%
 b) Assessment of Domain Knowledge and teaching Skills-30%
 c) Interview performance-20%
Associate Professor
 a) Academic records and research performance-20%
 b) Research performance based on API score and quality of
 publications- 40%.
 c) Assessment of domain knowledge and teaching skills-20%
 d) Interview performance-20%
Professor
 a) Academic records and research performance-20%
 b) Research performance based on API score and quality of
 publications- 40%
 c) Assessment of domain knowledge and teaching skills- 20%

11
 d) Interview performance-20%
However, the selection committee had acted with complete
arbitrariness in making self-styled norms in as much as the
following criteria were adopted (peruse Annexure-3.9):
 a) Academic records and research performance- valued at 45%
 b) Assessment of domain knowledge and teaching skills- valued
 at 20%
 c) Interview performance- valued at 35%
which is illegality manifest and apparent on the face of
record. Since the Annexure-3.9 is bulky, thus, for example is
quoted herewith for ready reference.

(ii) The above facts were also verified from the score sheet
which clearly provided that the selection committee had
adopted pick and choose method in awarding interview
marks, since the candidates better placed in academic
records, domain knowledge and teaching skills have been
awarded lesser marks in interview whereas the persons
having lower marks in academic records, domain knowledge
and teaching skills, have been given significantly higher
marks in the interview, thereby better choices have been
discarded.
The committee had placed the selection score sheet (as settled by
the selection committee) as per the AICTE/UGC norms for
Assistant Professors in the three disciplines of the writ petitioners
namely; Electronics and Communication Engineering, Civil
Engineering and Mechanical Engineering (presuming that the
candidate has got percentage of marks as given in score sheet), then
the situation emerging is mentioned in the score sheet (Annexure-3.10). Perusal of annexure-10 reveals that:
a) The petitioner No. 1, Mr. Ashutosh Tiwari was not
selected as Assistant Professor in Mechanical Engineering
by the ten selection committee as per the sheet annexed
herewith as Annexure-3.4. He would also fail to qualify
for selection in the panel if converting the score sheet
taken as per AICTE norms.

12
b) The petitioner No. 2, Mr. Dikenra Kumar Verma, was
selected as Assistant Professor in Electronics and
Communication Engineering as per the score sheet of the
selection committee. However, he would fail to qualify
for selection in the panel if converting the score sheet as
per AICTE norms, despite awarded highest marks in the
interview.
c) The petitioner No. 3, Mr. Mahavir Singh Rawat was
selected as Assistant Professor in Civil Engineering at the
second position as per the score sheet of the selection
committee. However, his merit would change to third
position if the score sheet taken as per AICTE norms
despite awarded second highest marks in the interview.
The above analysis is based on the AICTE norms nationally
applicable (explicitly mentioned in the advertisement itself).
Accordingly the cancellation of the candidature is amply justified
only on this ground itself. However, the marks of interview as
mentioned cannot be taken as justifiable, since the arbitrariness by
the selection committee is clearly visible.
9. The situation is visible in other branches also from perusal of
Annexure-3.8.
10. The committee have also gone through the recommendations
of the earlier committee report, in which the various
anomalies regarding roster of reservation, doubts on the
authenticity of the certificates of the two states and other
aspect have been pointed out.
However, this committee have also gone through
various other relevant aspects of the matter as mentioned
here in above.

The recommendation of screening committee was also not
proper since some of the candidates qualifying eligibility criteria
have even not been called for interview for example, Mr. Hitesh
Dimri in Mechanical Engineering (whose details are enclosed as
Annexure-3.11). It is also pertinent to mentioned here that conduct
of the screening committee shown that the said screening
committee not only withheld giving opportunity to the eligible
candidates for appearing before the selection committee for
selection and also deprived the institution to choose more
meritorious and appropriate candidates for the advertised post.
Since the act of screening committee is unjust, unfair and not
sincere, thereby vitiating the entire selection process at the very
inception.
Further, the process adopted by the selection committee is
also not proper because selection committee have changed criteria
laid down by the AICTE/UGC. On perusal of the record it appears
that the selection committee did not observe the principles of basic
fairness in selection process. It would also leave room for large
number of manipulations and malpractices, resulting into ultimate
damage to the interest of the institution and to the society at large,

13
consequently, damage to the public interest in the field of public
employment also. the committee is of the opinion that the entire
selection process is arbitrary, irregular, unjust, unfair, illegal and
malafide.
Accordingly, since the deserving candidates have been
discarded by the screening as well as selection committee, even
some of the eligible candidates were not called for interview and
roster of reservation not taken care of, it would be proper that the
entire selection process be cancelled. However, it would be proper
that a new selection process may be initiated by constituting fresh
screening/selection committee as per AICTE norms.

10. Thereafter, we also deem it appropriate to refer to the proceedings
of the 22nd Meeting of the Board of Governors in relation to Agenda Point
No. 22.02, which is the discussion and decision on the report of the Sub-Committee constituted in the 21st Meeting:
"Agenda Point No. 22.02: Discussion and decision on report of
Sub Committee constituted by the Board of Governors in its
21st meeting:
The Board of Governors have considered the report of the sub-committee constituted in its 21st meeting held on 2.04.2016 along
with the report of earlier enquiry committee regarding the
irregularities in the selection process for various, faculty positions
with respect to advertisement no. 01/faculty Admin/2013-14 dated
08.06.2013. The same was as per agenda point no. 21.01 duly
considered in the 21st meeting, as per decision of the Hon'ble High
Court of Uttarakhand in Writ Petition (S/B) No. 253 of 2015
wherein it is directed as under:
"........the Chairman has exercised power beyond the scope of the
authority conferred on him under the Byelaw in the facts of this
case. In such circumstances, we would think that the matter should
receive the attention of the competent body, namely, the Board of
Governors."

14
Further, in para 11 of the said judgment the Hon'ble Court has
directed as under:
".............The Board of Governors will consider the question as to
whether, having regard to the report submitted by the Committee
and any other relevant facts, the selection in regard to the posts, for
which the petitioners have offered themselves for selection, should
be cancelled......."
In the light of which a sub-committee was formed and its report is
placed before the Board of Governors. At the very outset it is made
clear that the relevant records/documents were produced by the
Registrar of the college, who, according to the bye-laws is the
Custodian of records/documents and solely responsible for the
authenticity/veracity and correctness of the same. The
recommendations of the sub-committee and enquiry committee
were point wise considered as under:
(i) Screening Process:
a. 04 candidates in Chemistry were called for interview but
they were not having qualification as per UGC 2009 norms.
b. 02 candidates in Mathematics were called for interview but
they were not having qualification as per UGC 2009 norms.
c. The Head of Applied Sciences and Humanities department
was not a member of screening committee for mathematics
which is a violation of College bye-laws being clause no.5
(a).
d. For the posts of Associate professor in mathematics,
ineligible candidates were called for interview but they were
not having minimum academic performance index of 300
points.
e. For the posts of Professor in MCA, ineligible candidates
were called for interview but they were not having minimum
academic performance index of 400 points.
f. For the post of Assistant Professor in ECE, the candidates
not having M. Tech degree in relevant field were also called
for interview. For this, the then Principal has changed
recommendations of screening committee.
g. For the post of Professor in ECE, the then Principal and
expert had changed recommendations of screening
committee to debar an eligible candidate to be called for
interview.

23. We have already noticed the relevant facts and the contentions.
The first question we must consider and decide is whether the procedure
adopted by the Board of Governors in the 21st Meeting in having two
persons as special invitees and, thereafter, constituting a committee,
which is treated as a Sub-Committee, consisting of four members

26
including the two special invitees, was legal. We have already set-out
bye-law 25(viii) of the Bye-laws and also bye-law 31(2)(d), which relates
to the powers of the academic committee. It is true that this Court had
directed the Board of Governors to take a decision, as it is the supreme
body in these matters, not being satisfied with the decision taken by the
Minister purporting to invoke his extra-ordinary powers. The Board of
Governors is, apparently, a large body. Apparently, it also consists of
bureaucrats and members of the academia. Bye-law 25(viii), in our view,
clearly clothes the Board of Governors with the power to constitute
special types of committees and the matter does not end there. The Board
of Governors is also empowered to constitute any other committee to
achieve any other object, which is specified by the Board of Governors.
Bye-law 25(viii) also empowers the Board of Governors to co-opt persons
into the committee. This is not to say that the academic committee is not
endowed with power under Bye-law 31(2)(d). The fact that the academic
committee can constitute a sub-committee or that it is to consist of experts
does not, in any way, whittle down the wide powers available with the
Board of Governors under Bye-law 25(viii). They are, in our view,
mutually exclusive and they deal with the power of two different
authorities. The power of the Board of Governors to constitute
committees, apart from the named committees, is clear. It also has a
power to co-opt persons into the Committee. Therefore, we are not
inclined to accept the case of the petitioners that the constitution of the
four-member committee in the 21st Meeting by the Board of Governors is
illegal. It may be true that the word "Sub-Committee" is missing in Bye-law 25(viii); but, in our view, it is beside the point and cannot advance the
case of the petitioners. This is for the reason that the purpose of
constituting a committee by a larger body, with which various powers are
given, is to enable the body to get inputs in the form of reports on the
basis of which it could take a decision. When a body constitutes a
committee, which it is entitled to do, and, thereafter, looks into the report
of the committee and takes a decision, the decision ultimately taken by the
Board of Governors, as in this case, would be the decision of the Board of
Governors. It has all the freedom to disagree with the decision of the

27
committee. In an appropriate case, after rejecting the report of one
committee, it may even be empowered to constitute another committee.
But, in no circumstances, could it be said that, for the reason that a
committee was constituted, which is characterized as a Sub-Committee,
the order of this Court directing the Board of Governors to take a decision
has been flouted, nor can it be said that the decision taken to constitute the
committee was unauthorized. Mere absence of the word "Sub-Committee" in Bye-law 25(viii), in our view, is not significant. The only
aberration, which we may note, is the participation of Additional
Secretary (Law) and an Advocate in the meeting of the Board of
Governors; but, we would think that they participated as special invitees
and, at any rate, we would rather judge this case on the more substantial
point, namely, whether the decision of the Board of Governors to cancel
the selection was based on material, which is relevant and which would
sustain its decision.
24. We would think that we would rest our refusal to interfere in the
writ petitions on one solitary ground. We say this, as, for instance, in
regard to eligible candidate like Hitesh Dimri being excluded from
consideration, there is much to be said against the Committee's report.
Hitesh Dimri, apparently, did not pass M.Tech. as on 04.06.2013. The
qualification prescribed for the post of Assistant Professor was B.Tech.
and M.Tech. in first class in the concerned discipline. Going by the
certificate dated 04.06.2013, it was issued only to vouchsafe the fact that
he had completed the course. Completing the course was not the
qualification, which was stipulated. Therefore, there may be merit in the
case of the petitioners that the Committee and the Board of Governors
were wrong in concluding that an eligible person in the form of Hitesh
Dimri was excluded. We notice that what the Committee has said is that
the name of Hitesh Dimri is taken as an example; but no other case is
forthcoming as such in the report of the committee.
25. Equally, in regard to the question relating to reservation of posts, no
doubt, in one of the branches (Mechanical Engineering), it is mentioned

28
that at least one woman candidate was available as against two posts. It is
not in dispute that, in the other two branches, no eligible woman was
available. It is also true that, in Electronics and Communication also,
there was a woman candidate available and she was, in fact, interviewed
also; but, only male candidates have been selected. Mr. Rakesh
Thapliyal, learned counsel for the petitioners, no doubt, points out that the
post in Electronics and Communication Branch was reserved for OBC
woman and there was no OBC woman candidate available.
26. That apart, we would, at any rate, think that the Committee has
come to the conclusion that, contrary to the stipulations of the AICTE, the
selection committee has acted illegally in allocating 35 per cent marks for
the interview, when the AICTE norms provide for 20 per cent marks. In
this regard, we must first consider the case of the petitioners that AICTE
norms are actually meant only for the purpose of career advancement
scheme. After perusing the Notification, while it is true that, on the first
page of the Notification, it deals with the issue relating to career
advancement; in the second page, it specifically deals with the criteria for
direct recruitment to the post of Assistant Professor, inter alia. Therefore,
we reject the said contention.
27. The next question we have to answer is whether Mr. Rakesh
Thapliyal, learned counsel for the petitioners, is correct in contending that
the norms evolved by AICTE are not binding and the University is free to
depart from them and that it has discretion in the matter. We are of the
clear view that, once the AICTE norms are prescribed and if the College
professes to follow the same, the institution is bound to follow the norms.
28. The third argument, which remains, is certainly the argument,
which is a vexed issue. True it is that AICTE has announced the criteria
to be followed in the case of Assistant Professor. We may, once again,
notice the criteria as part of our discussion. 50 per cent marks are devoted
to academic record and research performance; 30 per cent marks are to be
devoted to domain knowledge and teaching skills; and 20 per cent marks

29
are to be awarded for interview. There can be no dispute that, in this case,
contrary to this stipulation, the selection committee has allocated 35 per
cent marks for the interview. This is found to be a phenomenon, which
runs across the board in the selection to all disciplines and would certainly
be a factor, which will have its implication in all the writ petitions before
us. The Committee has found that the selection committee, by allocating
35 per cent marks in place of 20 per cent, has acted contrary to the
stipulations of AICTE, which we have found to be binding. It is also
found that persons with better academic record have performed not in
proportion to their academic attainments in the interview and the vice-versa is also found. In the view of the Committee and the Board of
Governors, which has accepted it, this was a factor, which has gone into
the decision making process leading them to cancel the selection.
29. The first question we must address and deal with is, what are the
contours of the Court's jurisdiction in interfering in such matters. It is
quite clear that we are dealing with this matter in judicial review. We are
addressing the issue in judicial review of administrative action. Judicial
review of administrative action is based on the writ court being not an
appellate court; but a court exercising supervisory jurisdiction. The three
well-settled heads under which interference can be legitimately premised
are illegality, irrationality and procedural impropriety. Coming under
these broad heads could be elements like violation of principles of natural
justice, bias, acting contrary to the law, in excess of law, acting under
dictation, fettering of discretion, abuse of discretion, non-application of
mind to relevant facts, proceeding on the basis of irrelevant facts and
mala fides. There have been two new recruits also, which have become
available to the courts, namely, the doctrine of legitimate expectation and
the doctrine of proportionality. But, running as a golden thread through
all these concepts is that, ordinarily, the writ court does not re-apprise the
findings of fact. It also would not interfere with a decision, if the decision
taken represents one of the views, which an authority can take. If it is, no
doubt, a view, which is so perverse that no person could take, the court
may strike it down. But, as part of the principle that the court does not act

30
as an appellate authority, if the view is a view which the authority could
reasonably take, though the court may think that there is a better view
which may be the view, which is advocated by the petitioners, the court
may still stay its hands and refuse to interfere. It is within the confines of
this jurisdiction that we must examine this last limb of the arguments of
the petitioners.
30. No doubt, we had directed the Board of Governors to take a
decision. In fact, there is no dispute regarding the fact that it is the Board
of Governors, which is the supreme body and which has to take the
decision. This is not a case, we must notice, where an unsuccessful
candidate, who is worsted in the selection, is before us and calling in
question the decision by the authority. We may probably have had
different considerations in such a circumstance. This is a case, where we
are being persuaded to interfere with the decision taken by the body,
which is admittedly competent to take the decision. The said competent
body has, indeed, spoken on the basis of material in the form of the
Committee's report. In regard to the case that is sought to be built-up by
the petitioners, which is apparently based on the certificate issued by the
Principal of the College, who was also, apparently, member of the
selection committee, we have noticed its contents. We have also noticed
the stand, which is taken by Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, learned counsel for the
petitioners, as to how the selection committee has, apparently,
apportioned the marks under various heads. We may notice a few
features. Under the 30 per cent marks, it is divided into two elements,
namely, domain knowledge and teaching skills. 20 per cent marks are
devoted for the interview. Admittedly, in violation of the same, 35 per
cent marks are given for the interview. The attempt appears to be that, as
far as domain knowledge is concerned, it is to be assessed and it can be
assessed in an interview. The selection committee is comprised of
experts. Apparently, they have drawn on their considerable experience.
Therefore, in the interview, they have found out domain knowledge on the
basis of the subject knowledge, which is indicated as one of the elements
in the certificate issued by the Principal. For the same, 15 marks may be

31
taken as granted. 20 marks, which are even otherwise available for the
performance in the interview, are devoted to the manner in which the
candidate gave the presentation and also discussion. Therefore, the 20
marks, which were intended to be given for the performance in the
interview, are given for the performance in the interview by way of the
manner in which the candidate made the presentation and the discussion.
As far as the teaching skill is concerned, he would submit that teaching
skill has been assessed by the teaching experience and also the possession
of Ph.D. He would, in fact, submit that most of the candidates, except
one, did not have Ph.D. and all have been treated equally in this regard.
Per contra, the case of the respondents appears to be that the court may
not miss the fact that, in the certificate issued by the Principal, the word
"presentation" is followed by an oblique (/) and, thereafter, followed by
group discussion and, finally, followed by subject knowledge. We will
proceed on the basis that the word "oblique (/)" is not intended to convey
the sense, which the respondents are intending, namely, that it is only
anyone of those; but the committee has employed all of those.
31. We, still, will be left with the following questions:
(i) Firstly, the question would arise whether the Committee has acted
legally in awarding 5 marks for Ph.D. under the category of 30 per cent
for domain knowledge and teaching skills. In fact, we find ourselves
unable to accept the case of Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, learned counsel for the
petitioners, that Ph.D. is assessed as part of teaching skills. In this regard,
he tried to draw sustenance from the fact that, in respect of IIT Indore, in
the Ph.D. programme which they have, the candidates, who are doing
Ph.D., would have to have teaching experience. What is provided in the
AICTE guidelines is teaching skills. We may, to a certain extent, agree
with the petitioners that teaching skills could be assessed with reference to
the quantitative data, namely, the number of years of experience that a
person may have; but, we find ourselves unable to accept the case that
Ph.D. as such would be a criteria for deciding the teaching skills. AICTE
has not provided for teaching experience or the number of years of

32
teaching. Instead, it has provided for teaching skills. Therefore, we do
not agree with Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal that teaching skills, per se, could be
ascertained from the question as to whether a person has Ph.D. or mere
teaching experience. The quality of teaching is as important, if not more,
as the number of years a teacher has taught. As to how it is to be
assessed, according to Mr. Paresh Tripathi, is through actual
demonstration of the teaching skills in front of a classroom. In this
regard, he would submit that this is provided in the UGC guidelines.
(ii) We further notice another aspect. In the certificate issued by the
Principal, there is reference to assessment of domain knowledge and
teaching skills based on higher qualification. It is, in fact, pointed out by
Mr. Subhash Upadhyaya that this concept of teaching skills based on
higher qualification is foreign to the stipulation by AICTE.
(iii) We may notice that, while it may be true that assessment of
teaching skills may probably be attempted in an interview and also even
domain knowledge may have to be assessed only in an interview, insofar
as the marks have been demarcated under various heads, namely, domain
knowledge and teaching skills under one sub-heading and the further sub-heading is interview, there has been no break-up of these marks. We may,
at once, record that we are conscious and we cannot be oblivious to the
fact that the selection process has been done by a group of experts. We
may, in fact, even go to the extent of noting that there may be merit in the
case of the petitioners that a group of experts must have free-play in its
joints and freedom to operate the criteria stipulated by the competent
body, which, in this case, is AICTE, as long as it acts within the four
walls of its powers; but, when certain questions, which we have noticed,
have arisen and what is far more important when the competent authority
has found it fit that the method adopted by the selection committee cannot
square with the requirement of the law, we need not interfere in exercise
of jurisdiction under Article 226.

33
(iv) In regard to the e-mail sent by one member of the Committee, we
would think that it is only one member, who has raised this issue and,
therefore, we need not fault the proceedings of the Board of Governors on
this basis. It is true that, though Mr. R.K. Singh had raised this
apprehension by the letter, he had participated in the subsequent meetings,
which agreed with the earlier meetings. In fact, it is pointed out that,
apart from Mr. T.N. Sharma, all the others have participated in the later
meetings.
32. In such circumstances, the writ petitions fail and are dismissed. No
order as to costs.
